header.title: Ad restringendum sanguinem [=Blutsegen, Erfurter] (Erfurt, Universitätsbibl., Cod. Ampl. 8° 62b): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Anonymous
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:rem:anonymous:m003:norm, from the Referenzkorpus Mittelhochdeutsch, ReM 2.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.69E.1: 'diz sîdin buozen' (69E.3-4) is read as 'diz sî dîn buozen', 'may this be your cure'; read as sîdîn it would be 'this silken ...'. 'habe dine s bluot' (69E.6) breaks off after s.

nodes.text: To staunch blood. In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Christ was
wounded; from that he was healed. Stand, blood! Stand, blood! Stand here
within, for the sake of holy Christ. The Our Father. May this be your
cure. Say this three times. Again: you see blood
flowing from an iron spring; that blood stood still when Christ
commanded: Stand, blood! Hold, blood! Hold your s..., blood! Holy
stand still, as the Jordan stood still, where Saint John baptised Christ, the Son of God.
The Our Father: these three times.
